stories.label: Brazil's Bolsonaro comeback exposes Lula's weakness
stories.summary: Follow-up to Sunday night's piece on the early count (one clause). The new development is the result: the first round is counted and Brazil goes to a runoff, with Flávio Bolsonaro, son of the jailed former president, ahead of Lula and called the favourite by Al Jazeera. Lead with the final first-round shares, the gap and the runoff date exactly as the reports give them, and with the congressional and governors' results if reported. The mechanism: a year after Jair Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years for plotting a coup, his family name won the first round, so say what the reports give as the cause (Lula's fading appeal, the economy, crime, which regions and voters moved) and what a Bolsonaro presidency would mean for his father's sentence. Take the facts from Al Jazeera and the FT; the FT piece is analysis, so quote its judgments as the FT's. RT frames the vote around alleged US and CIA meddling: it is Russian state media, and that claim goes in only as an attributed allegation with whatever evidence it cites, or not at all. Dateline Brasília.

stories.label: Ukraine claims Russia killed civilians in Black Sea ship attack
stories.summary: Two crew members died and 11 were rescued after a cargo ship caught fire and sank in the Black Sea close to Romania's shore on Monday; Zelenskyy says a Russian drone hit it. Lead with the dead, the rescued and the place as Romanian authorities give them, then Ukraine's accusation as an accusation: say what Romania itself has and has not attributed, and whether Moscow has answered or that it has not. Name the ship, its flag, its cargo and the crew's nationalities if the reports do; merchant crews in this war are mostly from countries far from it. The mechanism: the grain and cargo corridor along the Romanian and Bulgarian coast runs through NATO waters, so a strike there kills civilians under a NATO state's rescue responsibility and raises war-risk cost for every ship using it; give what the reports say on earlier attacks on the route. Take the facts from the AFP copy (Yahoo), NDTV and Ukrainska Pravda where Newsweek is thin. Dateline Constanța or Bucharest as the reports support.

stories.label: German spy chief warns of violent conflict risk with Russia
stories.summary: Martin Jäger, head of Germany's foreign intelligence service, the BND, told lawmakers on Monday that Russia's undeclared 'shadow war' is escalating and that Germany risks being drawn into a violent conflict. Lead with what he said under oath-like conditions to parliament, not with adjectives: the specific hybrid attacks he cited (sabotage, drones, arson, cyber, as the reports list them), any numbers, and what he asked lawmakers for. The mechanism: this is the annual public hearing where the services make their case for powers and money, so say what the BND wants and what the government is doing, and set it beside Estonia moving its main brigade to the Russian border (covered this morning, one clause). Give Moscow's reply as an attributed claim: RT is Russian state media and Anadolu is Turkish state media, so take the facts from the AFP copy carried by ANSA and from the Times of India, and nothing from RT the others lack. A warning, not an event: write it as testimony. Dateline Berlin.

stories.label: CIA Report Warns Israel Could Head Toward Civil War, Total Collapse
stories.summary: Drop Site reports that a CIA assessment warns Israel could slide into civil unrest, civil war or state breakdown around its 27 October elections. Lead with what the document is and how Drop Site knows of it (seen, described by sources, dated when), then its central judgment in the report's own terms. The mechanism: say which fractures the assessment names (the government and the security services, settlers and the army, the courts, conscription, the cost of three years of war) and what it says about the occupied territories and Gaza, where a breakdown of command lands first on Palestinians. This is one outlet's account of a classified document: attribute every claim to Drop Site and to the report as Drop Site describes it, state none as fact, and say whether the CIA, the White House or the Israeli government responded or declined. No second source in the feed carries it. The subject is Israel: dateline Jerusalem, with Drop Site reporting from Washington said in the text.

stories.label: Pakistan reports this year's sixth polio case
stories.summary: Pakistan has confirmed its sixth wild polio case of 2026, a seven-year-old child in Khyber district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the national polio emergency centre said on Monday. Lead with the child, the district and the count. The mechanism: Pakistan and Afghanistan are the last two countries where wild poliovirus still circulates, and the cases cluster in the districts where vaccinators cannot work safely or are refused; say what the NEOC statement gives on the child's vaccination history, where this year's other five cases were, how the count compares with last year's, and when the next campaign runs. A public-health report filed under politics, not science: there is no new finding here. Single source, the regional outlet. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: Replenishing crude, fuel supplies could take two years, Saudi Aramco CEO says
stories.summary: Distinct from this afternoon's piece on Kuwait's output and the fall in Brent crude (one clause): this is the world's largest oil exporter saying the shortage outlasts the war. Saudi Aramco chief executive Amin Nasser told the Energy Intelligence conference in London that the squeeze on crude and refined fuels will worsen, that refilling the emergency stockpiles drawn down since the war began could take two years, and, as The National reports, that Brent crude would have reached up to $200 a barrel without Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline. Lead with the two-year figure and the $200 claim, each attributed. The mechanism: the pipeline carries Saudi crude to the Red Sea around the Strait of Hormuz, which is why ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz can fall without Saudi exports stopping; governments covered the gap by emptying strategic reserves, and those barrels must now be bought back on top of normal demand, which holds the price of Brent crude up after the strait reopens. Say what he gives on pipeline volumes, stock levels and refined products ('both ends of the barrel'), and who it lands on: importers in Asia and Africa without reserves to draw. He runs a company that profits from high prices: write it as his assessment. The National added as the regional voice; it reports the same speech. The concept tag 'Gamal Abdel Nasser' is a mis-tag for Amin Nasser. Dateline London.

stories.label: Swiss president visits India to boost trade ties
stories.summary: India and Switzerland signed five pacts in New Delhi on Monday, two of them on the movement of professionals, and agreed to widen access for Indian exports to the Swiss market, as Narendra Modi and Swiss president Guy Parmelin also discussed defence and nuclear energy. Lead with what was signed, not the visit: the mobility agreements, the market-access terms and the investment-protection treaty Parmelin is pressing for, with figures where the reports give them. The mechanism: India's trade deal with the EFTA states came with a pledge of $100bn of investment over 15 years, and Switzerland wants legal protection for that money while India wants visas and market access for its workers and goods; say what each side got and what is still unsigned. One clause of context if the reports support it: India is closing deals with smaller partners while its trade talks with Washington are stalled. Take the Swiss side from Bluewin and the detail from the Hindustan Times; the Yahoo link is AFP. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: What will Washington do next if US bond yields keep rising?
stories.summary: Long-term US Treasury yields are near their highest in two decades and, Reuters reports, Washington is running out of easy ways to bring its borrowing costs down. Lead with the level of the US 10-year Treasury yield and the longer maturities as Reuters gives them, and with the cause: the volume of debt being sold to cover deficits, and inflation. The mechanism: say which tools the Treasury and the Federal Reserve have already used (shifting issuance to short-dated bills, buybacks, changes to bank capital rules, the Fed's balance sheet) and what each remaining option costs, as the report sets them out. Who it lands on: the US 10-year Treasury yield is the base rate for American mortgages and for dollar borrowing everywhere, so governments from Egypt to Pakistan to Nigeria refinance against it. Write it as reported facts and named options, not as a forecast; leave out analyst predictions. Single source. Dateline Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: A long and rocky road to ESG for Chinese overseas mining
stories.summary: Chinese mining companies operating abroad are moving towards international environmental and governance standards but lag on the social side, Dialogue Earth reports: labour conditions, community consent and grievance handling. Lead with the hardest evidence the report gives: a named company, mine or country, a ranking or audit, or a number. The mechanism: Chinese firms dominate the nickel, cobalt and copper that the energy transition runs on, in Indonesia, the Democratic Republic of Congo and elsewhere, and the pressure to raise standards comes from buyers, lenders and stock exchanges rather than from host-country law, which is why what can be audited on paper (emissions, disclosure) moves faster than what cannot (how workers and neighbours are treated); name the standards and the Chinese guidelines involved. Who it lands on: workers at nickel plants in Indonesia and communities around the mines. Write it as findings with their sources, not as a feature: no scene-setting. Single source; the feed has no Jakarta Post or other regional report. Dateline the country the reporting centres on.

stories.label: Denmark: Data of millions compromised in hack
stories.summary: Hackers broke into Denmark's national civil registry and compromised the records of some 8.8 million registered people, more than the country's living population, in what the authorities call an 'extremely serious' incident. Lead with the 8.8 million and what a record holds: the CPR personal identity number that is the key to Danish banking, health care, tax and digital ID. The mechanism for a technical reader: early findings say the intruders used the legitimate login credentials of a local company with access to the registry, so no vulnerability was needed; the weak point was a third party's account. Say what data was read or copied, for how long, who has been attributed if anyone, and what the minister (Christina Egelund is tagged) says the state will do, since a national identity number cannot be reissued like a password. If no attribution is given, say so and supply none. Single source. The concept tag 'Cardiopulmonary resuscitation' is a mis-tag for CPR, the registry. Dateline Copenhagen.

stories.label: Russian drones strike Ukraine's data centers by exploiting air defense gaps
stories.summary: A surge of Russian jet-powered drone strikes on Ukrainian data centres has cut mobile and internet service for thousands of people, and Zelenskyy and other officials are asking for more air defence to protect telecom sites. Lead with the strikes and the outages: how many facilities, which operators, how many people cut off, as Ars reports. The mechanism for a technical reader: jet-powered drones fly faster and higher than the propeller Shaheds that Ukraine's cheap interceptors and mobile gun teams were built to stop, and data centres are fixed, power-hungry and impossible to hide, so they sit in the gap between front-line air defence and the systems guarding power plants; say what was hit, how operators are rerouting or dispersing, and what a data centre's loss does to a country that runs its state services and its military logistics over the same networks. Give Russia's stated reason only if the report does. Single source. Dateline Kyiv, not a US dateline.

stories.label: Meta Rushed to Fix Muse ‘VM Escape' Vulnerability Soon Before Launch
stories.summary: Shortly before launching its Muse AI product, Meta rushed to fix a 'VM escape' vulnerability that could have let a Muse user reach sensitive internal Meta databases, 404 Media reports. Lead with what the flaw allowed and how close to launch it was found. The mechanism for a developer: an AI system that runs code or tools for a user does so inside a virtual machine or sandbox, and a VM escape means code inside that sandbox reaches the host and whatever the host can reach; say how the flaw was found (internal red team, employee, outside researcher), what it exposed, how it was patched and whether the launch date moved, from the documents or sources 404 Media cites. The accountability point: say what the report shows about the pressure to ship and what Meta said in reply, or that it did not comment. Give no technical detail the report does not. Original single-source reporting. Dateline Menlo Park. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: arXiv Is Rate Limiting Submissions Because It Can’t Keep up With AI Slop
stories.summary: arXiv, the preprint server where physics, mathematics and computer science publish first, is rate limiting submissions because its moderators cannot keep up: submissions have doubled in two years, which it attributes to AI-generated papers. Lead with the limit itself (how many papers, per author or per category, over what period) and the doubling. The mechanism: arXiv has no peer review, only volunteer moderators who check that a paper is plausibly scholarship, and that check was sized for humans writing at human speed; say what arXiv has already tried (the earlier restrictions on review and position papers in computer science, endorsement rules) and who the cap costs, which is prolific legitimate groups and researchers without institutional endorsers, many of them outside the US and Europe. Use 'AI slop' only as 404 Media's or arXiv's phrase. Single source. Dateline Ithaca, New York, where arXiv is run. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: Giorgia Meloni seeks to trademark her voice to counter AI deepfakes
stories.summary: Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni has applied to the EU Intellectual Property Office to register her voice as a trademark, filing four-second samples, to fight AI deepfakes before next year's general election. Lead with the filing and what it contains. The mechanism is the legal experiment: a sound trademark protects a sign used in commerce, not a person's identity, so say what classes she filed in, what a registration would let her do against a platform or a deepfake's maker that defamation, privacy or the EU's AI Act does not, and what lawyers in the report say about whether it can work. Note who else has tried it, if the FT does, and the precedent: if a head of government can own her voice as a mark, the same tool reaches satire and criticism as well as fraud. Single source. Dateline Rome.

stories.label: Automated vehicles drive safer but induce riskier behavior in human drivers in car-following scenarios - Communications Engineering
stories.summary: A study in Communications Engineering, a Nature Portfolio journal, finds that automated vehicles drive more safely themselves but that human drivers behave more riskily around them when following in traffic. Lead with the finding and its size, as the paper measures it (following distance, time headway, hard-braking or conflict rates), and say what data it rests on: the concept tags name Waymo and Lyft, so give the dataset, the cities and the number of interactions. The mechanism: say why the authors think humans tailgate or cut closer to a machine (it brakes predictably and never retaliates), and what that does to the safety case, since crash statistics that count only the automated car's own behaviour miss the risk it moves onto the drivers around it. State the limits the authors state: car-following only, observational data. This is an early-access accepted manuscript, peer-reviewed but not final: say so, name the journal exactly and do not call it Nature. Single source. No dateline country.

stories.label: Dozens quarantined in Siberia after plague institute lab worker dies
stories.summary: A worker at a plague research institute in Irkutsk, Siberia, has died of suspected pneumonic plague and dozens of contacts are quarantined. Lead with the death, the institute and the number quarantined, exactly as the reports give them, and say plainly what is confirmed and what is only suspected. The mechanism: pneumonic plague is the form that spreads person to person through the air and kills within days if untreated, so a laboratory infection is a biosafety failure, not a natural outbreak; say what the institute works on, what Russian authorities have and have not disclosed, and what the WHO or neighbouring states have been told. The Washington Post angle (the CDC and State Department seeking details) is one clause, not the story. Take the facts from Al Jazeera, Dawn and TRT World where the Post is paywalled; TRT World is Turkish state media but three independent outlets carry the same event. No speculation about a leak beyond what officials say. Dateline Irkutsk, Russia: not a US dateline.

stories.label: Yemeni army aims to regain control of entire country -- deputy defense minister
stories.summary: Follow-up to this morning's report that Saudi-backed government forces took positions at Dhubab on the Bab el-Mandeb coast (one clause). Two new developments since: the government has widened its stated aim from one front to the whole country, with deputy defence minister Samir al-Sabri saying the army intends to restore state control over every province while concentrating on Bab el-Mandeb and Mokha; and the Houthis have answered by telling airlines to avoid Saudi airspace, which their coordination centre says 'will become a theater of military operations'. Lead with the Houthi warning to civil aviation and the minister's declared aim, each attributed. The mechanism: a local offensive on the strait has become a declared war for all of Yemen with Saudi Arabia named as a target, which puts Gulf air routes and ship traffic through Bab el-Mandeb at risk at once; say what the SCMP reports the minister claims about control of the strait, what the Houthis hold, and what civilians in Taiz governorate face, only as reported. TASS is Russian state media relaying both statements: attribute by name and take the facts from the SCMP where it carries them. The National's piece is a who's-who explainer of the forces involved: use it for identifying the factions (Giants Brigades, the Presidential Leadership Council), and it is the regional voice. The second TASS link (Houthi airspace warning) was added to sources because the cluster did not include it. Dateline Taiz or Aden as the reports support; TASS files from Tunis and Doha.

stories.label: Matsda2sh journalists forced to read false ‘confessions’ statements to camera, subjected to torture in custody
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-04 report that Egypt's security prosecution detained Abu Emaira for 15 days while five other journalists from the fact-checking platform Matsda2sh were missing (one clause). The new development: the journalists have now appeared before prosecutors, and their lawyers from the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights say several were tortured at National Security Agency premises and forced to record false 'confessions' on camera. Lead with the allegation, who makes it (EIPR lawyers who attended Sunday's investigation sessions) and how many of the six it concerns. The mechanism: a filmed confession extracted before a detainee ever sees a prosecutor is evidence manufactured in the gap of enforced disappearance, and the target here is an independent fact-checking outlet; say what the charges are, what the prosecution ordered, what the journalists told investigators about their treatment, and whether the Interior Ministry or prosecution has answered, or that they have not. These are the lawyers' allegations: attribute them, and name the journalists as Mada Masr does. Single-source original reporting from the regional outlet. Dateline Cairo.

stories.label: BREAKING: 32 people on board crashed Nigerian military aircraft - Aviation Minister
stories.summary: A Nigerian Air Force aircraft with 32 people on board crashed on Monday at Igbokoda, in Ilaje local government area of Ondo State, on what the air force calls a routine flight from Benin to Lagos. Lead with the crash, the place and the number aboard as aviation minister Festus Keyamo gave it, and give casualties only if and as the reports do: if no toll is confirmed, say so. Then what is known: the aircraft type, who was on board (military personnel or others), the state of the search and rescue the air force says it has activated in a riverine area. The mechanism, only as far as the report supports it: the Nigerian military's record of fatal air crashes and what investigation has been ordered. Do not supply a cause. The two Premium Times items are one event: the minister's figure and the air force statement. This is an accident, filed under politics, not science. Dateline Igbokoda, Nigeria.

stories.label: Two men executed in Iran over role in killing police officers
stories.summary: Iran executed two men on Monday, named by the judiciary's Mizan agency as Alireza Sepahi and Alireza Raisi, over the killing of four police officers during the unrest early this year. Lead with the two names, the execution and the charge, attributed to the judiciary. The mechanism: these are executions arising from protests, carried out in wartime, and the only account is the state's; say what court convicted them, on what charge, whether the Supreme Court upheld the sentences, and how many protest-related executions this makes, only as the report gives it. The sole source is Mehr, an Iranian state-affiliated agency relaying the judiciary: write 'Iranian state-affiliated agency Mehr reported', attribute every claim, and do not adopt its words 'terrorists' or 'foreign-orchestrated riots' except in quotation. Say plainly that the feed carries no account from the men's lawyers, families or rights groups, and no independent confirmation of the trial's conduct. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: Oil drops as Hormuz traffic rebounds
stories.summary: Follow-up to this morning's shipping-data piece on Middle East crude exports (one clause). The new development is a producer's own number and a price move: Kuwait is pumping about 2 million barrels a day, roughly 75% of its pre-war rate, as more tankers risk the Strait of Hormuz, the chief executive of Kuwait Petroleum Corporation said, and Brent crude fell on the rebound in traffic. Lead with Kuwait's figure and the Brent crude move as Bloomberg and Semafor give them. The mechanism: Kuwait has no pipeline around the strait, so its output is a direct measure of ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz; say how the barrels are getting out, and set beside it Al Jazeera's question of whether Iran is charging a toll for passage, with what evidence and whose denials. Who it lands on: a Gulf state still missing a quarter of its oil income, and Asian importers paying war-risk freight. Give prices and volumes only as reported. The New Arab link is analysis: quote it as a named view, not as fact. Al Jazeera and The New Arab are the regional voices. Dateline Kuwait City; the remarks may have been made at a conference in London, so follow the report.

stories.label: Why is PTC stock surging today? By Investing.com
stories.summary: The story is the deal, not the share price in the feed headline: France's Schneider Electric agreed on Monday to buy the US industrial-software company PTC for about $22.6 billion, the largest acquisition in its history, to build up its data-centre business. Lead with buyer, target and price, then the market's verdict: Schneider's own shares fell sharply, as Euronews reports, while PTC's rose. The mechanism: the company that sells the power and cooling gear for AI data centres is paying a record sum for the design and engineering software used to plan them, a bet that the building boom lasts long enough to repay it; say how the deal is financed, what premium Schneider is paying, and why its shareholders balked. Who it lands on: a European industrial group taking on debt for an American software asset, and the regulators on both sides who must clear it. Aol carries the Reuters report; take the facts from it, Euronews and CNA, and nothing from Investing.com beyond the share move. Dateline Paris: not a US dateline.

stories.label: NNPC revenue plunges by N10.6trn in 2025
stories.summary: Nigeria's state oil company NNPC Limited lost almost a quarter of its revenue in 2025: its audited accounts show group revenue down 23.4% to N34.52 trillion from N45.08 trillion, driven by a 77.6% collapse in income from petroleum products. Lead with the N10.56 trillion fall and the 77.6% figure. The mechanism is the surprising part: say why product revenue collapsed, as Premium Times explains it (NNPC ceasing to be the country's sole fuel importer as the Dangote refinery and private marketers took over supply, or whatever the accounts state), and what happened to profit, crude sales and remittances to the federation account. Who it lands on: the federal and state governments that depend on NNPC's payments, and through them the naira. Accountability: this is the first full picture of a company long criticised for opaque accounts, so say what the auditors flagged, if anything. Single-source reporting from the regional outlet on audited figures; give numbers only as the report does. Dateline Abuja.

stories.label: SEC approves first 3x bitcoin and ether ETFs in the U.S.
stories.summary: A regulatory decision, not a price story: on 2 October the US Securities and Exchange Commission approved a Cboe BZX rule change allowing six exchange-traded funds from Volatility Shares that aim to deliver three times the daily move of bitcoin, ether and the other assets the report names, the first triple-leveraged crypto ETFs in the United States. Lead with the approval and what the products do. The mechanism a technical reader wants: a 3x daily fund resets every day using derivatives, so over weeks its return decays away from three times the asset's and a one-day fall of a third wipes it out; say what limits or disclosures the SEC attached and how this follows the agency's wider loosening on crypto (one clause: the OKXICE tokenized-stock filing covered this morning). Who it lands on: retail buyers, who are the market for these funds. This concerns bitcoin: give its price only as CoinDesk reports it. The piece is a daily market briefing: take the SEC decision and leave the rest; no investment framing. Single source. Dateline Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Japanese media group Nikkei discloses cyberattack targeting journalistic sources
stories.summary: Nikkei, the Japanese media group that owns the Financial Times, has disclosed a breach of an employee's email account that may have exposed journalists' sources. Lead with what was accessed and why it matters more than an ordinary corporate breach: the data at risk is the identity of people who spoke to reporters. The mechanism: say how the account was compromised as The Record reports it (phishing, stolen credentials, malware), how long the intruder had access, what Nikkei says was and was not taken, and whether anyone has been attributed; if Nikkei gives no attribution, say so and supply none. Note Nikkei's earlier incidents if the report recalls them. Who it lands on: sources in Japan and abroad who were promised confidentiality, and what Nikkei says it has told them. The feed entry is a teaser (thin): write only from the fetched article. Single source. Dateline Tokyo.

stories.label: The AI boom is making the world’s cheapest smartphones disappear
stories.summary: AI data centres are buying up so much memory that phone makers are raising prices and dropping their cheapest models, Rest of World reports. Lead with the hardest number the report gives: a price rise, a discontinued model line, or the share of memory output now going to data centres. The mechanism: the same few manufacturers make DRAM and NAND for servers and for handsets, server memory pays far more, so capacity moves to AI and the cost of the memory in an entry-level phone rises until the phone is not worth making; name the chipmakers and the phone brands (Transsion, Xiaomi, Samsung or whichever the report names) and the markets. Who it lands on: first-time internet users in Africa, South Asia and Southeast Asia, for whom a sub-$100 handset is the only way online. Write it as reported findings, not a feature. The feed entry is a teaser (thin): write only from the fetched article. Single source. Dateline the country the reporting centres on, not the US.

stories.label: Iran able to disable Starlink operations during war
stories.summary: Distinct from this morning's piece on Tehran summoning Norway's ambassador over Starlink (one clause). The new claim is technical: the secretary of Iran's Supreme Cyberspace Council, who also heads the National Cyberspace Centre, says Iran managed to control and block some networks and platforms, Starlink among them, during the war. Lead with the claim and who makes it. The mechanism for a technical reader: say exactly what he says was done and how (jamming of the user downlink, GPS spoofing that stops terminals locating themselves, seizures of terminals), and be plain about what the report does not establish: no figures, no independent measurement, no response from SpaceX. Set the two facts side by side: a state that says it can switch Starlink off is the same state protesting diplomatically that it cannot stop it. The only source is Mehr, an Iranian state-affiliated agency: write 'Iranian state-affiliated agency Mehr reported', attribute every claim to the official by name, and state none as fact. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: China and the race to fish a tiny animal with a vast climate role
stories.summary: Antarctic krill, a thumb-length crustacean, moves large amounts of carbon to the deep ocean and feeds the whales, seals and penguins of the Southern Ocean, and China is expanding its fleet to catch more of it. Lead with the science the report rests on: how much carbon krill are estimated to sink each year and by what route (faecal pellets and moulted shells), with the study or researchers named. Then the pressure: the size of the catch, China's share and its new vessels, and the catch limit set by the Antarctic conservation commission CCAMLR, whose members meet this month, where proposals for protected areas have been blocked. The mechanism: the limit is set for the whole region but the fishing concentrates in the small areas where predators feed, so a catch that is legal overall can strip a local ecosystem. Give the industry's case (a protein and omega-3 source) as the report does. Write it as findings and decisions, not as a feature: no scene-setting. Single source. Dateline none beyond the Southern Ocean unless the report gives one.

stories.label: Saudi-backed Yemeni forces seize vital strait from Houthi rebels
stories.summary: Follow-up to the government's declaration of an operation against the Houthis and the explosions near a tanker off Mokha (both covered 10-04, one clause each). The new development is territory: Yemeni government troops backed by Saudi Arabia say they have taken positions at Dhubab on the Bab el-Mandeb coast from the Houthis. Lead with what was taken, by whom and from whom, and write it as the government's claim where Al Jazeera does ('claim to seize'); give the Houthi account or say there is none. The mechanism: whoever holds the Dhubab shore holds the launch sites that threaten ship traffic through Bab el-Mandeb, so say what the FT and Al Jazeera report about shipping, Saudi air support and the role of Rashad al-Alimi's government, and what the fighting costs civilians in Taiz governorate, only as reported. Al Jazeera is the regional voice. Dateline Dhubab, Yemen, or Taiz if the reports file from there.

stories.label: Spanish PM Sanchez calls snap election
stories.summary: Follow-up to the housing protests and Valencia clashes after Congress rejected the government's tenant protections (covered 10-03 and 10-04, one clause). The new development is the decision yesterday's piece only asked about: Pedro Sánchez has called a snap election. Lead with the announcement and the date, then why now. The mechanism: a minority government that could not pass its housing bill has chosen the ballot over governing without a majority, with the far-right Vox positioned to gain; say what the report gives on polls, coalition arithmetic and the scandals that weakened him. One clause on what is at stake outside Spain: Sánchez has been the EU leader most outspoken on Palestinian statehood. Daily Maverick carries Reuters copy; single source. Dateline Madrid.

stories.label: "Modified Form 6 not approved by us": CJI observes on modified form for enrolling new voters
stories.summary: Follow-up to three days of protests demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's removal, with about 500 detained in Delhi (covered 10-04, one clause). The new development: the fight has reached the Supreme Court, where Chief Justice Surya Kant said the court never approved the modified Form 6 used to enrol new voters and asked who changed it, while declining to pass orders against Kumar on the basis of media reports. Lead with the court's statement that the form was not its doing. The mechanism: Form 6 is the gate to the electoral roll, so an unauthorised change to it during the Special Intensive Revision decides who can vote; say what was changed in the form, what the petitioners allege against Kumar, what the Election Commission answered, and what the bench ordered or listed next. Observations from the bench are not a ruling: write them as such. All three sources are Indian. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Estonia actively redeploying troops to Russian border -- FT
stories.summary: Estonia is moving its 1st Brigade, the main combat-ready part of its land forces, to a newly expanded base less than 50 km from the Russian border, its commander Tarmo Kundla told the Financial Times. Lead with the move and the distance. The mechanism is a change of doctrine: a small NATO state is abandoning the plan of trading ground for time until allies arrive and instead placing its army to fight at the border from the first hour; say what Kundla gives as the reason, where the base is (Jõhvi and Narva are tagged), and what it implies about confidence in reinforcement. Give Moscow's reading as attributed claims only: TASS and RT are Russian state media, and RT frames the story around missiles aimed at St Petersburg, so take the facts from the Kyiv Independent's account of the FT interview and nothing from RT the others lack. Dateline Tallinn, or Jõhvi if the report places the base there.

stories.label: Reconciliation not possible without including Imran, PTI says
stories.summary: Follow-up to the PTI protest march from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (covered 10-04, one clause). The new development: talks between the government and the PTI collapsed over the weekend, and the party's leaders, secretary general Salman Akram Raja among them, now say no reconciliation is possible unless the jailed Imran Khan is part of it. Lead with the failure of the talks and the condition. The mechanism: the government is negotiating with a party whose leader it holds in prison, so say what each side offered and why it broke down, as PTI narrates it and as the government answers. Set beside it federal minister Amir Muqam's statement the same day (second Dawn link) that Islamabad does not favour governor's rule in KP but sees security risks from the march: the threat of suspending an elected provincial government is the lever on the table. Attribute each side's account. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: Kremlin declines comment on report that Ukraine talks are linked to multi-billion dollar oil deal
stories.summary: The New York Times reports that US-Russia talks on ending the war in Ukraine have widened to include a multibillion-dollar oil deal; the Kremlin declined to comment on the report, while spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed that energy cooperation is under discussion. Lead with what the reported deal is (Lukoil and Jared Kushner are tagged: say who would buy or operate what, only as Reuters relays it) and with Peskov's non-denial. The mechanism: a peace negotiation in which the mediator's envoys are also negotiating commercial energy terms, days after Zelenskyy offered trilateral talks this month and two weeks before Washington's 18 October date for secondary sanctions on buyers of Russian oil (both covered 10-04, one clause each); say what the deal would mean for sanctions on Russian crude and so for Brent crude. A report and a refusal to comment, not a confirmed agreement: write it as such, and include Kyiv's and Washington's responses or say Reuters has none. Single source. Dateline Moscow.

stories.label: More Qatari LNG cargoes transit Strait of Hormuz despite ongoing risks
stories.summary: Distinct from this morning's piece on crude exports (one clause): this is gas. More liquefied natural gas cargoes loaded at Qatar's Ras Laffan reappeared outside the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend, extending a recent rise in Qatari LNG traffic through a waterway Iran says is shut. Lead with how many cargoes got through and how Reuters knows (ship-tracking data: tankers go dark inside the strait and reappear outside it). The mechanism: Qatar cannot bypass Hormuz by pipeline as Saudi crude can, so every LNG cargo is a transit under risk; say where the cargoes are headed, how the volume compares with before the war, and what that does to natural gas prices for the Asian and European buyers who depend on it. This is about ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and the price of natural gas: give figures only as reported. No Gulf outlet in the feed reports the data. Dateline Ras Laffan, Qatar; Reuters files from Singapore.

stories.label: Euro zone business growth hits over 3-1/2-year high despite inflation worries, PMI shows
stories.summary: Euro zone business activity grew in September at its fastest pace in nearly three and a half years, the S&P Global PMI survey shows, while the same survey recorded resurgent price pressures from the Middle East war. Lead with the headline index and the price readings as Reuters gives them. The mechanism: strong demand plus rising input costs is the combination that keeps the ECB rate going up, and the European Central Bank has already been raising it; say what the survey shows on prices charged, which countries and sectors drove the growth, and what economists in the report expect the ECB to do next. Who it lands on: borrowers and households in the euro area paying for an energy shock twice, at the pump and through the ECB rate. A survey, not official output data: say so. Single source. Dateline Frankfurt or Brussels as the report supports; Reuters files from Bengaluru.

stories.label: Nobel prize in medicine 2026 awarded for research on mysteries of brain
stories.summary: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine went to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for light-gated ion channels and optogenetics. Lead with the three names and, in one plain sentence, what they made possible: switching chosen neurons on and off with light. The mechanism is the science, not the ceremony: Hegemann and Nagel characterised channelrhodopsins, light-sensitive proteins from green algae that open an ion channel when lit; Deisseroth put the gene into mammalian neurons so that a pulse of light fires a specific cell type. Say what that let researchers establish that electrodes and drugs could not (cause, not correlation, in circuits for movement, memory, fear), and what has reached patients so far, such as the partial restoration of vision in a blind patient, only as the sources report. Note who is not on the list if the reports raise it; the three-laureate limit has been argued over for this field for years. Prize money 12m Swedish kronor. Dateline Stockholm.

stories.label: The US Companies Cashing In on the Ukraine War
stories.summary: Beyond American weapons, a set of US technology companies now supply the war in Ukraine with software, data, satellite and AI services, Inkstick reports. Lead with the named companies and what each sells to whom, with contract values where the report gives them; if it names none, the piece is not worth writing. The mechanism for a technical reader: a battlefield is the proving ground and the sales pitch, so say what systems are being fielded (targeting, drone autonomy, satellite links, data fusion), who pays (Kyiv, Washington, European donors), and what the firms take away in data and in follow-on contracts with other governments. The accountability gap: say what export control or oversight applies to software and models as opposed to munitions, as the report describes it. Write it as reported findings, not as a feature, and attribute characterisations such as 'cashing in' to Inkstick. Single source. Dateline Kyiv, not a US dateline.

stories.label: Iran studying US response to its 7-day proposal
stories.summary: Follow-up to Iran's statement that Hormuz stays shut until seven conditions are met, with reopening within seven days (covered 10-04, one clause). The new development: Washington has answered. Deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi says Tehran is reviewing the US response to its 7-day plan to end hostilities and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Lead with the fact that a reply exists, who delivered it and through whom (Qatar is tagged), and what either side has disclosed of its content; if nothing is disclosed, say so. The mechanism: the plan trades a ceasefire and sanctions relief for ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, so say which of the seven conditions the reports name as sticking points. Set beside it Araghchi's line to ambassadors on Sunday, as Dawn reports it, that Iran is serious about diplomacy and that a renewed military path would bring a firmer response. A review, not an agreement: write it as such. Tabnak is an Iranian outlet close to the establishment; take the facts where TimesNow, Telangana Today or Dawn also carry them. Dawn added as the regional voice (its piece is the Araghchi speech on the same talks). Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: US: FBI arrests woman accused of spying for China
stories.summary: The FBI arrested a California woman at Los Angeles airport before she could board a flight to Shanghai, accusing her of surveilling the son of Taiwan's president and his family on China's behalf. Lead with who was watched and where: a foreign head of state's family, tracked on US soil. The mechanism: the charge is acting as an unregistered foreign agent (the Foreign Agents Registration Act is tagged), not espionage, so say exactly what she is charged with, what the complaint alleges she did and for whom, and what her lawyer or Beijing says in reply; an accusation is not a conviction. Context in one clause: the arrest comes soon after Xi's visit to Washington, and the reports frame it against lingering US-China tension. Take the facts from DW, Al Jazeera and Nikkei where the Bloomberg text is short. Dateline Los Angeles, or Seattle if the reports place the case there. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Ethiopia's forces retake Mekelle amid renewed Tigray fighting
stories.summary: Ethiopian federal forces and allied Tigray Peace Force fighters have captured Mekelle, the capital of Tigray, in renewed fighting with the TPLF. Lead with the fall of the city, who took it and from whom. The mechanism: the 2022 Pretoria deal that ended a war which killed hundreds of thousands left the TPLF split and its relationship with Addis Ababa unresolved, and the federal government is now fighting alongside a Tigrayan faction against the party that ran the region; say who the Tigray Peace Force is, what role Eritrea is reported to play, and what residents told Al Jazeera about displacement, services and food. Give casualties and the state of the city only as reported, and say what the TPLF and the federal government each claim. Single source filing from Addis Ababa, not Mekelle: say so if access to the city is restricted. Dateline Mekelle if the report supports it, otherwise Addis Ababa.

stories.label: Sudan's RSF Refused to Rescue Dozens in Gold Mine Collapse Where at Least 82 Died, Survivors Say
stories.summary: At least 82 people died when an informal gold mine collapsed in Sudan, and survivors say the Rapid Support Forces, who control the area, refused to mount a rescue for dozens trapped underground. Lead with the dead, the place and the named actor, and attribute the refusal to the survivors Drop Site interviewed. The mechanism: both the RSF and the Sudanese army fund the war from gold, so informal mines run without engineering, safety or rescue capacity under the armed group that taxes them; say who ran this mine, where the gold goes, and what the RSF says in reply, or that it did not respond. Distinct from the Dilling drone strikes covered 10-04 (no more than a clause). Single-source original reporting; give numbers only as the report does. No Radio Dabanga or other regional report of the collapse in the feed. Dateline the mine's locality as the report names it.

stories.label: Iran's oil minister resigns, no reason given
stories.summary: Iran's oil minister Mohsen Paknejad has resigned and President Pezeshkian's office has replaced him with Hamid Bovard, head of the National Iranian Oil Company, with no reason given. Lead with the resignation, the replacement and the absence of an explanation. The mechanism: the ministry is the one that has to sell crude through a US blockade of Iran's oil exports, and the change comes the same weekend the state gas company admitted a drop in South Pars output (covered 10-04, one clause); say what Reuters reports about export volumes and revenue under the blockade, and whether parliament must confirm the successor. Do not supply a motive the sources do not give. The statement originates with Iranian state media via the president's office: attribute it. Take the facts from Reuters and NDTV; the Times of Israel link is a live-blog entry. No regional outlet beyond the state statement in the feed. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: Middle East crude oil exports exceed pre-war levels but tanker attacks increase
stories.summary: Shipping data show crude exports from the Middle East rose above pre-war levels on four of the last seven days of September, even as attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz increased. Lead with that paradox and the figures Reuters gives. The mechanism: say how the barrels are moving, as the report explains it (which exporters, which routes, pipelines that bypass the strait, escorted or dark transits), and what the rise in attacks does to freight and war-risk insurance, because that cost is why Brent crude has stayed high while volumes recover. This is about ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and the price of Brent crude: give the daily transit and export numbers and the Brent level only as reported. Context in one clause each: Iran says the strait stays shut pending its seven conditions, and explosions were reported near a tanker off Mokha on 10-04 (both covered). Who it lands on: Asian importers, where the cargoes go. Reuters copy carried by Nikkei; no Gulf outlet in the feed reports the data. No dateline country to count against the US cap; Reuters files from Singapore.

stories.label: Steep fuel price rise close to midterms forces one-third of US states to cut taxes
stories.summary: About one-third of US states have cut fuel taxes or eased diesel restrictions as pump prices climb weeks before the 3 November midterms, a domestic bill for the war with Iran. Lead with the number of states and the size of the price rise in gasoline and diesel as the report gives it (AAA figures). The mechanism: states are giving up road-fund revenue to mask a price set by crude and by a diesel shortage that tax holidays do not fix, so say which states acted, what each cut costs, and what economists in the report say about whether the saving reaches drivers. This bears on US inflation and follows from the price of Brent crude: state those links only with the figures the report supplies. One clause of context: Trump's proposed $5,000 checks (covered 10-04). Dawn is carrying wire copy from Washington. Dateline Washington. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: New forensic evidence supports Egyptian "retainer sacrifice"
stories.summary: A forensic re-examination of remains from First Dynasty royal burials, more than 500 years before the Great Pyramid, supports the long-disputed idea that servants and officials were killed to be buried with the earliest pharaohs. Lead with what the new analysis found on the bones (the skulls are tagged) and why it settles more than the old argument from suspiciously simultaneous burials. The mechanism: say which remains were studied (Flinders Petrie's excavated collections), what forensic method was applied, what marks or patterns indicate killing rather than natural death, and how many individuals show it; then what stays uncertain, in the researchers' own terms. Name the team and the journal as Ars Technica reports them. A finding, not a museum piece: no scene-setting. Ars Technica is the full report; the Phys.org entry is a teaser of the same study. Dateline Abydos, Egypt, if the report names the site, otherwise the research institution.

stories.label: Associations between vaccine misinformation and influenza vaccine uptake: a population-based interrupted time-series study in China - npj Digital Public Health
stories.summary: Researchers matched large-scale vaccination records in Zhejiang, China, against the timeline of online vaccine-misinformation events and found flu vaccination fell or slowed after them. Lead with the measured effect: how much uptake dropped, after which kinds of events, and for how long, as the paper reports. The mechanism is the method: an interrupted time-series design compares the trend in real vaccination records before and after each misinformation event, so this is behaviour, not survey answers; say which groups were most affected and what the authors say they cannot establish (association in time, not proof of cause). Why it matters to a general reader: most evidence on misinformation and vaccines is from the US and Europe and from stated intentions. The paper is in npj Digital Public Health, a Nature Portfolio journal, not Nature itself: name the journal correctly. Dateline Hangzhou only if the paper gives the institution there; otherwise none beyond Zhejiang.

stories.label: Tehran summons Norwegian envoy over Starlink
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry summoned Norway's ambassador to protest what it calls Norway's continued inaction over unauthorised Starlink activity on Iranian territory. Lead with the summons and the obvious question it raises: why Norway, for a US company's satellites. Answer it only from the report (Norway's role in the relevant international body, licensing or ground infrastructure, whatever the ministry cites). The mechanism for a technical reader: satellite internet bypasses the state's control of the national network in wartime, a terminal needs no local licence to work, and the only levers a government has are diplomatic and regulatory complaints against the states that register or host the service; say what Iran is asking Norway to do and under which rules. The only source is Mehr, an Iranian state-affiliated agency, reporting its own foreign ministry: attribute every claim by name, state none as fact, and note the feed carries no Norwegian or SpaceX response. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: OKXICE files for 24/7 tokenized trading in 60 U.S. stocks
stories.summary: OKXICE, a joint venture of the crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange, the owner of the New York Stock Exchange, has filed to offer round-the-clock trading in tokenized versions of 60 US stocks. Lead with who is filing and what would trade. The mechanism a technical reader wants: say what a tokenized share is here (who holds the underlying stock, on which chain the token settles, what rights the holder has), and what makes it legal, namely a new five-year SEC exemption, with a 30-day window in which companies can object to their shares being tokenized. Who it lands on: issuers who did not ask for it, and retail buyers trading outside the hours when the main market sets the price. A filing, not a launch: say what regulatory steps remain. No investment framing. Single source. Dateline New York. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: Results trickle in as Brazil awaits results of high-stakes election
stories.summary: Follow-up to this morning's report that Brazil was voting (one clause). The new development is the count: Senator Flavio Bolsonaro took an early lead over President Lula as first-round results began to come in on Sunday afternoon. Lead with the latest tally each source gives, the share counted, and whether a runoff is now certain (a candidate needs over 50%; say the runoff date). The mechanism: early returns in Brazil come disproportionately from particular regions, so say which states had reported and what the sources say about where the remaining votes are - do not call a winner the sources do not call. Then what is at stake beyond the presidency: Congress and the governors elected the same day, and the Trump administration's open backing of the Bolsonaro camp, as Reuters, the BBC and Al Jazeera report it. Yahoo carries Reuters copy; RT is Russian state media - take nothing from it the others lack. Dateline Brasília.

stories.label: US removes all bombers from RAF Fairford back to home stations
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-01 report of a British-Iranian man arrested over an incident at RAF Fairford (one clause). The new development is a decision: a US official confirmed on Sunday that all American bombers - B-1s, per the reports - have been withdrawn from the Gloucestershire base to their home stations, while counter-terrorism police investigate the alleged Iran-linked plot. Lead with the withdrawal and who confirmed it. The mechanism: Fairford is the forward base from which US heavy bombers fly missions in the Iran war, so a suspected plot on British soil has, in effect, moved part of the US strike force out of Europe - say what reason the US gave (security, or a routine rotation), what the Pentagon and the UK government each say, and what the police have and have not alleged. Allegations stay allegations: no charge is a conviction. The Jerusalem Post and India Today frame it as an Iranian plot; take the facts from the BBC, NYT and SCMP. Dateline Fairford, England - not a US dateline.

stories.label: US execution survivor critically ill on ventilator, lawyer says
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-01 report that Tennessee's attempt to execute Christa Pike with pentobarbital failed (one clause). The new development: Pike is critically ill and on a ventilator, her lawyer says, days after the state injected her at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville and she did not die. Lead with her condition and who reports it, then what the state has said about what went wrong and whether it intends to try again. The mechanism: a single-drug pentobarbital protocol is presented as a painless medical procedure, but it is carried out without doctors and with drugs from undisclosed suppliers - say what is known about the dose, the IV placement and how long the attempt lasted, strictly as the BBC reports, and what the governor and the courts have done since. Take the facts from the BBC; the NYT link is an opinion piece by an anaesthesiologist who consulted on her case - quote him only as a named expert with that interest stated; the Times of Israel link is a live-blog entry. Dateline Nashville. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Israeli Authorities Trade Blame for Failure to Flag FlyDubai Co-Pilot
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-03 reports that identified the Flydubai co-pilot accused of attacking his captain with the cockpit axe and noted he had earlier been barred from flying (one clause). The new development is the accountability fight: Israeli agencies are now blaming one another for failing to flag a man already deemed a security risk before he was rostered on a flight to Tel Aviv. Lead with which bodies are named and what each says the other should have done. The mechanism: crew on flights into Israel are vetted through lists passed between the airline, the UAE and Israeli security services, so say where, on the sources' account, the earlier bar over alleged 'extremist' views was recorded and why it did not stop him - a gap in data-sharing between states that normalised ties, not one man's act. Give the UAE and Flydubai positions as reported; 'extremist' is the authorities' word, so attribute it. No regional outlet beyond Al Jazeera in the feed. Dateline Tel Aviv.

stories.label: Ukraine ready for US-backed talks with Russia: Zelenskyy
stories.summary: Follow-up to the strike on Kyiv's Northern Bridge during Merz's visit and Moscow's vow to step up strikes (both covered today - one clause each). The new development: at the news conference with Merz, Zelenskyy said Ukraine is ready for trilateral talks with the United States and Russia this month and backs a swift timeline. Lead with the offer and its terms - when, where (the UAE is tagged) and at what level, as Al Jazeera reports. The mechanism: the offer comes in the same week both sides declared escalation and two weeks before Washington's 18 October date for secondary sanctions on Russia's trade partners, so say what Zelenskyy is asking of Washington and what, if anything, Moscow and the White House have answered; if there is no Russian response in the report, say so. A statement of readiness, not an agreed meeting - write it as such. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: BiH Central Election Commission announced preliminary results of general elections
stories.summary: Bosnia and Herzegovina voted in general elections on Sunday, and the Central Election Commission's preliminary count has Denis Bećirović of the Social Democratic Party leading the race for the Bosniak seat on the three-member presidency with 38.12%. Lead with the preliminary figures for all three presidency seats (Bosniak, Croat, Serb) and the share of votes counted, exactly as the commission gives them. The mechanism a reader needs: the Dayton constitution splits the presidency by ethnicity and the country into two entities, so say who leads in Republika Srpska, where the secessionist question sits, and what the result means for a state whose Muslim plurality shares power by treaty. Preliminary numbers only - call no winner the commission has not. The sole source is TASS, Russian state media, filing from Belgrade and relaying the commission: attribute by name, take the figures and none of the framing. No regional or independent outlet in the feed carries the result. Dateline Sarajevo.

stories.label: Multiple explosions reported near tanker off Yemen: UKMTO
stories.summary: The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported on Sunday that a tanker detected multiple explosions close to the vessel about 60 nautical miles south of Mokha, Yemen - on the approach to Bab el-Mandeb. Lead with the incident, the position and what UKMTO says about the ship and crew. The mechanism: this comes the day Yemen's government declared an operation against the Houthis and days after three commercial vessels were struck near Hormuz (covered - one clause each), so both of the region's chokepoints are now under fire at once; ship traffic through Bab el-Mandeb and the Suez route behind it is what is at risk, and with it the insurance and freight cost carried by Brent crude. Say whether anyone has claimed the attack; if not, say so and attribute nothing. The fact comes from UKMTO, relayed by Mehr, an Iranian state-affiliated agency: attribute to UKMTO via Mehr by name. The feed cluster is mislabelled ('Iran war to end very soon: Trump') - the Dawn and Middle East Eye links are context on the wider war and the earlier Hormuz strikes, the MEE one a live-blog entry; use Trump's remark in one clause only if Dawn reports it. Dateline Mokha, Yemen - not a US dateline.

stories.label: Mark Kelly calls Trump's $5,000 check plan a "payoff"
stories.summary: An economy story, not a talk-show quote. Trump has proposed sending a $5,000 check to every adult American if Republicans keep control of Congress in the 3 November midterms; Senator Mark Kelly said on CBS's Face the Nation that it is an attempt to 'buy votes'. Lead with the proposal itself and its condition - payment contingent on an election result - then Kelly's charge. The mechanism: say what the plan would cost and how it would be paid for, only as Newsweek reports (tariff revenue, borrowing, or unstated), whether it needs an act of Congress, and how it follows the $90 checks to Medicare seniors (covered 10-03 - one clause). Who it lands on: a transfer of that size bears on US inflation and on the US 10-year Treasury yield through the borrowing it implies - state that as the question economists raise only if the report does. Give the White House's defence in its own words. Single source; Kelly is a partisan opponent, so attribute his characterisation. Dateline Washington. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: Trump Accord Enshrines Light-Touch Regulation of AI
stories.summary: Distinct from the AI czar appointment covered this morning (one clause). Two linked facts: Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to replace the term 'artificial intelligence' with 'super intelligence', and an accord with the industry that, on the Daily Caller's account, enshrines light-touch regulation; Elon Musk has answered by saying SpaceXAI will be renamed SpaceXSI. Lead with what the order and the accord actually bind anyone to - which agencies, which companies signed, what rules are waived or pre-empted - and treat the rename as the visible symptom, not the story. The mechanism: the administration is setting AI policy by voluntary accord and vocabulary rather than statute, days after OpenAI's safety departures, so say what obligations on testing, disclosure or liability the accord contains and what it leaves out; if the reports give only the branding, say so plainly. The Daily Caller is a partisan outlet favourable to the administration and the Economic Times is reporting Musk's post: attribute each, state no characterisation as fact. Dateline Washington. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: UK's Green Party adopts 'Zionism is racism' policy
stories.summary: Members of the Green Party of England and Wales, meeting at conference in Brighton, passed a motion declaring Zionism a form of racism and backing a single Palestinian state. Lead with what the motion actually says and commits the party to, the vote margin if reported, and how leader Zack Polanski (who is Jewish) responded. The mechanism: this is a members' vote binding party policy, not a leadership statement, in a party now polling as a serious rival to Labour on the left — so say what changes in practice. Give the objection in its own words (the Movement for Progressive Judaism and other Jewish community leaders call it antisemitic and say it discriminates against Jewish supporters) and the proponents' case in theirs; the sentiment split between FT and MEE/Dawn/SCMP is the story's two readings, so attribute each. TRT World is Turkish state media; FT, Dawn and SCMP are the factual base. The MEE link is a live-blog entry — use it only for quotes. Dateline Brighton.

stories.label: 500 detained in Delhi on Day 3 of protests seeking CEC's exit; Thackerays lead Mumbai march
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 160 detentions at the Delhi march against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar (10-03) and the journalists' harassment complaints (this morning) — one clause each. The new development: on day three the number detained in Delhi rose to about 500, and the protest spread to Mumbai, where Uddhav and Raj Thackeray led a 'Garjana Morcha' demanding that the Special Intensive Revision of the voter rolls be scrapped and paper ballots replace EVMs; Mumbai police have filed an FIR over the march. Lead with the 500 and the spread to a second city. The mechanism: the SIR lets the Election Commission strike names from the rolls ahead of state elections, so the fight is over who is allowed to vote, and the state's answer so far is detention and criminal cases against organisers — say what the Commission and the government say in reply, and give figures on names removed only as the sources report them. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Chaos in Spain as anti-tourist protests turn into violent clashes
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-03 report on the marches after Congress rejected the Sánchez government's tenant protections (one clause). The new development: Saturday's protests ended in clashes with police in Valencia, and the defeat of the housing bill has opened the question of an early election — Al Jazeera asks whether Sánchez's minority government can survive it, and unions are talking of a general strike. Lead with the clashes (arrests and injuries only as reported) and the political consequence, not the crowd. The mechanism: rents are rising faster than wages while tourist lets take housing off the market, and a government without a majority has just shown it cannot legislate on it — say what Sánchez and his allies have said about an election and what the tenants' unions will do next. Use Al Jazeera for the facts and the politics; the Express is a tabloid ('chaos' and 'anti-tourist' are its words — the protests are about housing), and RT is Russian state media: take nothing from either that Al Jazeera, Yahoo Finance or News18 does not also report. Dateline Valencia, or Madrid if the reports centre there.

stories.label: India In Talks With Both Russia And Ukraine To End War: S Jaishankar
stories.summary: External affairs minister S Jaishankar said on Sunday that India's approach to the Russia-Ukraine war has moved 'beyond advocacy' of dialogue and that New Delhi is in talks with both Moscow and Kyiv — the clearest signal yet that India may mediate. Lead with his exact words and what, concretely, India is doing (contacts, visits, proposals — only as reported); if it is words alone, say so. The mechanism: India is one of the few states with working ties to both sides and is the largest buyer of Russian seaborne crude, which gives it leverage with Moscow and exposes it to the US secondary sanctions Washington is weighing — so mediation is also self-interest. Say what Moscow and Kyiv have said in the past few days about India's role, as the reports give it. Context in one clause: the week's escalation in Kyiv (covered). Both sources are Indian; the feed carries no Russian or Ukrainian response to this statement, and the article should say so. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Over 800 Palestinian teachers killed in Israeli attacks since Gaza genocidal war
stories.summary: Ahead of World Teachers' Day (5 October), the Palestinian Education Ministry said Israel has killed more than 800 Palestinian teachers, injured over 3,300 and detained more than 170 since October 2023. Lead with the three figures and who counts them. The mechanism: killing and detaining teachers, on top of destroyed schools, removes the people an education system is rebuilt from — give the ministry's figures on schools, students and lost school years only as the statement states them, and say whether the count covers Gaza alone or the West Bank too. Not a re-run of this morning's Gaza City strike (one clause at most): this is the cumulative toll on one profession. Say whether a ceasefire is nominally in force, as the report gives it. The only source is TRT World, Turkish state media, relaying a Palestinian Authority ministry: attribute the figures to the ministry via TRT by name, and note that the feed carries no Israeli response. Dateline Ramallah, where the ministry sits, unless the report says otherwise.

stories.label: Yemeni government announces launch of operation against Houthis
stories.summary: Follow-up to this morning's report of government strikes on Sanaa and Saada (one clause). The new development is a decision: Yemen's internationally recognised government has formally announced an operation against the Houthis, saying it is moving 'from the stage of preparations to the stage of liberation' after exhausting peaceful options — while the Houthi military spokesman claims advances against Saudi-backed forces in al-Jawf. Lead with the declaration, who made it and what it commits to; then the Houthi claim, as a claim. The mechanism: the truce that froze Yemen's front lines is now over in name as well as in fact, inside the wider US-Iran war, and the people who pay are Yemenis in a country where most already depend on aid — give casualties and territory only as reported. Both sources are state media on opposite sides: TASS (Russian state agency, filing from Doha) for the government's announcement, Mehr (Iranian state-affiliated, which calls the Houthi forces 'the Yemeni Armed Forces' and their opponents 'mercenaries') for the Houthi claim. Attribute each by name, adopt neither's vocabulary, and say nothing here is independently confirmed. Dateline Aden, the government's seat, unless the report says otherwise.

stories.label: Sudan Doctors Network: Four civilians killed in RSF drone attacks on South Kordofan
stories.summary: Rapid Support Forces drone strikes on residential neighbourhoods of Dilling, South Kordofan, killed four civilians, including a child and a woman, the Sudan Doctors Network says. Lead with the dead, the town and the named actor — the RSF — and who is doing the counting: a doctors' network, because no state body is. The mechanism: Dilling has been under siege and drones now let the RSF hit a town it does not hold, so civilians are killed at home with no front line near them; give the number injured, the dates of the strikes and the state of the town's hospital and supplies only as Radio Dabanga reports. Say what the network demands and whether the RSF has responded. Dateline Dilling.

stories.label: Security prosecution detains Abu Emaira for 15 days, whereabouts of 5 other Matsda2sh journalists unknown
stories.summary: Follow-up to the disputed detention order for six Matsda2sh journalists and the open-ended sit-in at the Journalists Syndicate (both covered 10-03 — one clause each). The new development: one of the six has surfaced. Mohamed Ashraf Abu Emaira was brought before Egypt's Supreme State Security Prosecution at 10 pm on Saturday, five days after his arrest, and given a 15-day detention order, an Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights lawyer told Mada Masr; the other five are still unaccounted for. Lead with the first appearance and the five still missing. The mechanism: five days of unacknowledged custody before any prosecutor is seen is enforced disappearance in practice, and State Security Prosecution's renewable 15-day orders can hold a journalist for years without trial — say what he is accused of, as the lawyer reports it. Matsda2sh is a fact-checking platform: say what it published. Dateline Cairo.

stories.label: Hailstorms destroy 3,750 farms in South Darfur
stories.summary: Hailstorms destroyed at least 3,750 farms in the Daous area north-west of Kass, South Darfur, the locality's executive director told Radio Dabanga. Lead with the number of farms and what was growing on them, weeks before harvest. The mechanism: in a region where war has already cut planting, markets and aid access, a lost harvest is not replaced — these families have no insurance, no state compensation and limited relief, so say which crops were lost, how many people depend on them and what help the official asked international organisations for, strictly as reported. Who administers Kass (South Darfur is under RSF control) matters for whether aid can reach it: state it if the report does. A disaster report with consequences for hunger, not a weather story. Dateline Kass.

stories.label: US doesn't rule out imposing secondary sanctions on Russia's trade partners by Oct. 18
stories.summary: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the administration does not rule out deciding by 18 October to impose secondary sanctions on Russia's trade partners, under the sanctions law Trump signed on 18 September. Lead with the date and whom it lands on: not Russia but the countries that buy its oil — India, China and Turkey above all — whose refiners and banks would have to choose between Russian crude and access to the US market. The mechanism: say what the law requires by that date and what discretion the president keeps, as the report gives it; with Hormuz restricted, discounted Russian barrels are what several importers are leaning on, so the threat bears on Brent crude as well as on Moscow's revenue. Wright's remarks are a statement, not a decision — write them as such, and include his line that ending the war would lower energy prices only as attributed. The only source is TASS, Russian state media, reporting a US official's remarks: attribute by name and say where he made them. Dateline Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Fuel supply stable despite South Pars output drop: NIGC
stories.summary: The head of the National Iranian Gas Company, Saeid Tavakoli, acknowledged that production at South Pars — the field that supplies most of Iran's natural gas — fell in the first six months of the Iranian year, while saying deliveries to power plants and industry held. Lead with the admission, not the reassurance: give the size of the drop and its stated cause if he gives them, and say so plainly if he does not. The mechanism: South Pars feeds Iran's power stations, industry and home heating, so lower output heading into winter means the choice between cutting industry, burning dirtier liquid fuel in power plants or rationing households — say how the company claims it kept supply stable (storage, fuel switching, cuts elsewhere) as reported. One clause of context: the war and the US blockade. The only source is Mehr, an Iranian state-affiliated agency, quoting a state company about its own performance: attribute every figure to Tavakoli via Mehr, and state none of the 'stable supply' claim as fact. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: One giant clam contains a month‑by‑month diary of the Great Barrier Reef's climate 200 years ago
stories.summary: Researchers have read a month-by-month record of the Great Barrier Reef's climate about 200 years ago from the shell of a single giant clam. Lead with what the shell recorded and for how long. The mechanism is the story: a giant clam lays down shell in fine growth bands, and the chemistry of each band (oxygen isotopes and trace elements, as the report specifies) fixes the temperature and conditions of the water it grew in — so one shell gives monthly resolution from before instrument records began, where corals and ice cores give coarser or more distant readings. Say how the shell was dated, what the record shows about reef conditions then against now, and name the team and the journal as Phys.org gives them. A finding, not a nature piece: skip the scene-setting about swimming over the reef. The feed entry is a teaser — use only what the page states. Dateline as the report gives the research institution; Townsville or Cairns only if stated.
